environment.description: Same IoT gateway code deployed on EKS (1.28) behind an Istio 1.20 service mesh with AuthorizationPolicy enforcing RequestAuthentication. The Istio RequestAuthentication resource specifies jwksUri pointing to an internal JWKS endpoint that ONLY serves the RSA public key, with fromHeaders extraction. The mesh-level RequestAuthentication has jwtRules with a forwardOriginalToken: false setting and outputClaimToHeaders mapping. Critically, the Envoy sidecar's jwt_authn filter is configured with 'providers' that enumerate ONLY RS256 in 'from_headers' with payload_in_metadata, and the filter's 'rules.match.requires.provider_name' references this single provider. The AuthorizationPolicy then requires the presence of request.auth.claims[device_id] which is only populated when Envoy's jwt_authn filter successfully validates against the RSA JWKS. Any token using HS256 algorithm will fail Envoy-level validation before reaching the application container, as the jwt_authn filter does not list HS256 in its accepted algorithms and the JWKS endpoint has no symmetric key material. Additionally, the pod's ServiceAccount has no access to the HMAC secret volume mount (projected volume restricted via PodSecurity admission with a baseline profile that blocks hostPath, and the secret itself is in a different namespace accessible only via a NetworkPolicy-gated internal API).

config.authorization_policy: ALLOW only when request.auth.claims[device_id] is present
config.hmac_secret_access: Secret in security namespace, pod ServiceAccount has no RBAC binding to read it, projected volume not mounted in gateway pod
